reason: Pi 1.5.2 reads before_agent_start prompt additions only from the systemPromptOptions object it passes in (runner.js emitBeforeAgentStart). Returning systemPrompt instead flattens the sectioned prompt and drops other extensions' sections.
Same host contract as above, for the prompt sections.
JSON.parse throws on a malformed credentials file and has no non-throwing form. The catch returns undefined, which callers read as "no credentials"; a throw would abort the job start.

lstatSync throws ENOENT, ENOTDIR and EACCES for a missing or unreachable path. The catch returns false (not a symlink) for all of them; { throwIfNoEntry: false } would still throw for ENOTDIR and EACCES.
mkdirSync is the atomic lock and throws EEXIST when another holder has it. The catch also covers any error from the locked function and returns false; the finally releases what was taken.
The catch returns the job report with a 'could not be restarted' note as the tool/wake text; it must not throw because the report would be lost.
The watcher reports a step failure through ctx.ui.notify and keeps polling. Throwing would kill the watcher loop; console.error would corrupt the TUI.
The catch removes the half-created job directory and rethrows the original error unchanged, so the tool error text Pi shows is exact. A console.error would add stderr output in the TUI.
A launch failure is recorded into the job's output with exit code LAUNCH_FAILED_EXIT_CODE and the function returns false; throwing would skip settling the job, and console.error adds stderr.
readFileSync and JSON.parse throw for a missing, unreadable or malformed job.json, and neither has a non-throwing form. The catch returns undefined so job listing skips it.
process.kill(pid, 0) throws ESRCH or EPERM and is the only liveness probe that needs no child process. The catch returns false (wrapper gone), which the stop logic depends on.
claimWake creates the woken marker with flag wx, which throws EEXIST once the wake was claimed. The catch returns false so each wake is delivered once; no non-throwing exclusive create exists.
A worktree failure returns a { refused } result whose message is sent to the requester; it must not throw, and the message is existing output.
readFileSync and JSON.parse throw for a missing, unreadable or malformed granted.json. The catch returns [] (no grants); throwing would break requests without grants.
A launch failure is settled into the job output with EXIT_LAUNCH_FAILED and serving continues; throwing would stop the broker, and logging adds stderr.
One failing request must not stop the others (documented); the catch swallows by design.
readFileSync throws EACCES, EISDIR and similar, with no non-throwing form. The catch returns undefined and discovery skips the file.
existsSync passed, but readdirSync still throws ENOTDIR or EACCES, with no non-throwing form. The catch returns [] (no agents) instead of failing discovery.
statSync throws ENOENT, ENOTDIR, EACCES and ELOOP, while { throwIfNoEntry: false } covers only ENOENT. The catch returns false (not a directory) for all of them.
JSON.parse throws on a non-JSON stdout line and has no non-throwing form. The catch returns { success: false } and the line is ignored while streaming.
The catch swallows every error from statSync, readRange and the onChunk callback, not only ENOENT, so the poll loop never dies on one bad chunk. Narrowing it would change that.
lstatSync throws ENOENT, ENOTDIR and EACCES. The catch returns false (absent) for all of them; { throwIfNoEntry: false } would still throw for ENOTDIR and EACCES.
readdirSync and lstatSync throw EACCES, ENOENT and the like, with no non-throwing form. Without repair the catch returns no value; with repair it falls through to the chmod retry.
The retry after chmod can still throw; the catch returns { unreadable: [path] } so the sweep reports and quarantines it. Throwing would abort the sweep.
renameSync has no non-throwing form. The catch copies across devices only for EXDEV and rethrows every other error unchanged; a console.error would add stderr text in the sweep process.
A quarantine failure is appended to the job's output file with a specific message and returns false; throwing would abort the sweep, and the message is existing output.
A sweep failure is appended to the job's output file as a message; the process must still exit normally, and logging adds stderr.

lstatSync, readdirSync and readFileSync throw for a missing or unreadable session directory or file, with no non-throwing form. The catch returns undefined (no report); throwing would break job reports.

Any failure to start the tmux session, including the synchronous ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE Node throws for a NUL byte in the model-supplied cwd, becomes spawnError, which the subagent tool reports as 'Failed to spawn subagent: <message>'. Without the catch that NUL case throws out of the tool instead, and console.error plus a new Error would change the reported message and add output to Pi's terminal.
